notice: Curated candidate catalog. Documentation review is not a security audit or performance benchmark. Prices must be checked before recommending a purchase. No affiliate ranking.

tools.name: Your existing coding assistant
tools.why: Try the assistant and tools you already have before adding another subscription.
tools.tradeoff: Usage limits and model costs still apply. Independent review and external evidence may require other tools.
tools.setup: Use the prepared workflow in your existing client. Check which search, browser and review tools that client actually provides.

tools.name: Firecrawl hosted API
tools.why: Candidate for structured collection from multiple public web pages.
tools.tradeoff: Check credits, site access, API costs, and whether existing browser/search tools are sufficient.
tools.setup: Read current official setup instructions and choose only the collection scope needed for the research.

tools.name: Penpot
tools.why: An open-source design candidate when the task needs editable design assets and a shared visual system.
tools.tradeoff: Self-hosting creates maintenance work; hosted service terms and integration details need verification.
tools.setup: Choose hosted or self-hosted deployment, establish visual requirements, then verify the current agent integration.

tools.name: Playwright
tools.why: Inspect and test the actual browser experience rather than judging generated source alone.
tools.tradeoff: Browsers consume local resources. Tests need task-specific assertions and maintenance.
tools.setup: Use the official CLI or MCP integration supported by the host. Review browser results against the product brief.

tools.name: Semgrep Community Edition
tools.why: Candidate for deterministic local static checks alongside an assistant review.
tools.tradeoff: Rules and language coverage vary; static scans do not replace human or architectural judgment. Verify metrics, rule downloads and data flow. Use local rules and disable metrics when external connections are prohibited.
tools.setup: Verify current language/rule support and run a scoped local scan before adding it to CI.

tools.name: CodeRabbit
tools.why: Candidate when integrated PR review is valuable to the team's actual workflow.
tools.tradeoff: Check current plans, review coverage, code access and pricing before comparing against local checks or existing-agent review.
tools.setup: Compare the same representative PR against the existing review process before subscribing or replacing it.

tools.name: GitHub Actions
tools.why: Automate repeatable checks close to the repository when GitHub is already in use.
tools.tradeoff: Runner minutes, storage and account terms can create charges; workflows require maintenance.
tools.setup: Reuse relevant existing checks. Verify current billing and repository permissions before adding jobs.

tools.name: Superpowers
tools.why: Candidate for structured planning, implementation and review workflows in an existing coding assistant.
tools.tradeoff: Extra workflow steps and agents consume time and model usage; evaluate whether that overhead helps this task.
tools.setup: Use current client-specific installation instructions. Start with one relevant workflow.

tools.name: Promptfoo
tools.why: Evaluate a proposed prompt or model change on representative inputs.
tools.tradeoff: Model calls for evaluations may cost money; quality criteria still need to be defined for the product.
tools.setup: Create a small task-specific dataset and compare the existing and proposed approach under the same conditions.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.why: Candidate for understanding which AI calls drive cost, latency and failures.
tools.tradeoff: Hosted service pricing or self-hosting operations add cost. Trace content can include sensitive data.
tools.setup: Choose deployment and data capture deliberately. Tag requests by feature before using cost summaries.

tools.name: PostgreSQL
tools.why: A database candidate when relational data and existing team skills fit the product.
tools.tradeoff: Operating a database includes backups, updates, availability and recovery responsibilities.
tools.setup: Define the data model and recovery needs, then compare managed and self-operated options.

tools.name: Supabase
tools.why: Compare a combined database, authentication and storage platform with separate services.
tools.tradeoff: Verify current limits, deployment choices, region, data policies and growth costs. Bundling is not automatically cheaper.
tools.setup: Choose the required services only and verify access controls with the actual tenant/data model.

tools.name: Neon
tools.why: A managed PostgreSQL candidate to compare against the project's current database arrangement.
tools.tradeoff: Check compute, storage, transfer, region and account limits at the intended usage.
tools.setup: Model the workload and verify current connection and pricing guidance before migrating.

tools.name: Cloudflare Workers
tools.why: A deployment candidate when runtime and application requirements fit.
tools.tradeoff: Runtime limits, data placement, integrations and usage pricing need verification.
tools.setup: Check runtime compatibility and estimate requests, compute, storage and transfer before deployment.

tools.name: Vercel
tools.why: A deployment candidate when preview workflows and supported application frameworks fit the project.
tools.tradeoff: Verify commercial terms, seats and metered compute/transfer at the expected workload.
tools.setup: Compare a preview deployment with the current host using the same application and usage assumptions.

tools.name: PostHog
tools.why: Measure the user behavior needed to judge a launch or product experiment.
tools.tradeoff: Event volume and enabled products can affect cost. Only collect data the project needs.
tools.setup: Define the decision and events first, then check current pricing and data handling requirements.

tools.name: n8n
tools.why: A workflow automation candidate for repeated handoffs across services.
tools.tradeoff: Compare execution pricing, license terms and self-hosting maintenance with a small script or scheduled job.
tools.setup: Map triggers, inputs and side effects. Build and test a single bounded workflow first.

tools.name: Resend
tools.why: An email delivery candidate when transactional email is required.
tools.tradeoff: Check volume, domain setup, retention and current pricing. Delivery provider choice does not solve messaging strategy.
tools.setup: Establish domain authentication and test a transactional message before connecting production events.

tools.name: A small script or scheduled job
tools.why: Consider a small local operation when the task is narrow and an automation platform would add overhead.
tools.tradeoff: Someone must own scheduling, credentials, retries, errors and maintenance.
tools.setup: Specify inputs, output, retries and the failure path. Keep the operation narrow and observable.

tools.name: Direct customer interviews and a small validation experiment
tools.why: Collect evidence about a specific customer's recent problem before buying a larger research stack.
tools.tradeoff: Requires recruiting and interpretation. A few interviews are not proof of a whole market.
tools.setup: Ask about actual behavior, alternatives and costs; record evidence and unresolved assumptions.
